title: Skeleton State Authority and Persistence Topology
purpose: Define which physical stores exist, which logical state domains they host, which state is authoritative versus derived/scratch/recovery-only, and the migration/backup/rebuild rules for each.
principles: storage technology does not define authority
derived indexes are rebuildable projections and never the only source of canonical state
scratch state can be discarded without corrupting canonical user or engine state
authoritative durable state has an explicit migration, backup, restore, retention, and consistency contract
recovery snapshots are evidence or recovery aids unless explicitly promoted by contract
one logical state domain has one canonical authority at a time
mixed-authority stores are transitional and require an explicit open construction gap

physical_stores.network: internal application network; host binding is loopback-only
physical_stores.restore: must be proven before production promotion
physical_stores.migration: logical databases have independent migration/rebuild policy

physical_stores.production_role: application-local persistent support data; currently includes local Chroma
physical_stores.backup: required only for any state not yet migrated to an authoritative document store; target is derived-only
physical_stores.restore: rebuild derived indexes from authoritative sources after state-authority convergence
physical_stores.migration: remove authoritative product state from local Chroma before treating volume as rebuildable

physical_stores.network: internal network; host binding loopback-only; optional full profile
physical_stores.authentication: no application auth boundary in compose; never public
physical_stores.backup: optional when fully derived; rebuild is preferred
required only if selected as production operation-event authority
physical_stores.restore: reopen database and preserve exact-next sequence, compaction watermark, terminal fence
physical_stores.migration: schema migration required before changing durable event/head tables

physical_stores.technology: SQLite canonical operation repository plus transactional outbox
physical_stores.production_role: reference authoritative operation state with atomic event-intent outbox
physical_stores.backup: required when selected as production operation authority
physical_stores.restore: reopen database, verify identity digests/state/version, then resume unpublished outbox delivery
physical_stores.migration: schema migration must preserve operation identity, monotonic state/version and deterministic outbox identity

physical_stores.production_role: cache, working memory, deterministic local index, reference implementation
physical_stores.restore: rebuild from authoritative sources or start empty

physical_stores.backup: not a substitute for authoritative store backup
physical_stores.restore: explicit opt-in restore into memory planes
physical_stores.migration: snapshot format compatibility required before durable operational use

physical_stores.technology: planned durable execution repository; production binding not yet materialized
physical_stores.production_role: future authoritative storage boundary for AI execution, turn/checkpoint, approval, idempotency, usage and final-result state
physical_stores.network: in-process repository contract until production adapter is selected
physical_stores.authentication: inherits orchestration/tool authority and tenant binding
physical_stores.restore: unimplemented until production repository binding; recovery semantics are defined in the cognitive runtime blueprint
physical_stores.migration: future repository schema must preserve execution/turn identity, checkpoint fencing, approval binding, idempotency reservations, usage monotonicity and final-result terminality

state_domains.transaction_scope: Mongo document/transaction boundary as implemented by domain repositories
state_domains.consistency: primary application state; writes must not be acknowledged as durable if Mongo commit fails
eventual regeneration acceptable; must not be required as sole user-state authority
state_domains.migration: skip application-state migration and rebuild from reviewed seed/content sources

state_domains.consistency: loss may cancel/recompute work but must not corrupt canonical app state
engine durable writes require Mongo acknowledgement
state_domains.backup_restore: required before relying on engine Mongo state in production

state_domains.consistency: retrieval projections may be rebuilt; authoritative user progress/feedback must migrate to canonical document state
state_domains.backup_restore: temporarily preserve until authoritative records are migrated; target rebuildable-only
state_domains.migration: move user_progress, feedback, session ownership and other canonical product records to Mongo; retain Chroma embeddings/projections only

state_domains.consistency: eventually consistent projection; absence must degrade retrieval, not canonical state

state_domains.transaction_scope: BEGIN IMMEDIATE operation transition plus transactional outbox intent
state_domains.consistency: legal monotonic state transitions, optimistic version fencing, terminal finality, idempotency identity and atomic outbox intent
state_domains.retention: operation/governance lifecycle controlled; durable deployment policy still required
state_domains.backup_restore: required when selected as production operation authority; reference reopen/recovery is tested
state_domains.migration: preserve operation identity digest, state/version monotonicity and unpublished outbox rows

state_domains.consistency: exact-next monotonic sequence; duplicate identity conflict rejection; terminal finality
state_domains.backup_restore: required if selected as production stream authority; otherwise conformance/reference only

state_domains.consistency: point-in-time best-effort capture of selected in-memory planes
turn index and checkpoint version are monotonic; only one resumable canonical checkpoint may be current for an execution
state_domains.backup_restore: required after durable repository binding; restore must recreate exact latest committed checkpoint and turn lineage
state_domains.migration: must preserve operation_id, execution_id, turn_id lineage, checkpoint version and terminal execution state

state_domains.logical_location: tool call reservation / execution receipt by operation_id + call_id
state_domains.consistency: one call_id has one canonical reservation and terminal receipt; a completed side effect is never executed again during replay
state_domains.retention: at least as long as the operation/result remains replayable or auditable
state_domains.migration: preserve call_id, arguments digest, idempotency mode, fence/version, status, receipt and compensation metadata

state_domains.logical_location: approval record bound to operation/execution/turn/call and arguments digest
state_domains.transaction_scope: request/decision/expiry transition for one approval identity
state_domains.consistency: approval applies only to the exact arguments digest and authority context; edited or expired requests require a new approval
state_domains.retention: auditable through operation lifecycle and applicable governance retention
state_domains.migration: preserve approval identity, arguments digest, risk class, requester/decider identities, expiry and decision

state_domains.logical_location: per-operation/per-turn estimated and actual resource consumption
state_domains.transaction_scope: monotonic append/update of normalized usage deltas
state_domains.consistency: consumed budget cannot decrease; unknown actual usage is explicit and never normalized to zero
state_domains.retention: billing/telemetry policy controlled; aggregate retention may exceed raw execution-detail retention
state_domains.backup_restore: required when used for quota/billing/release evidence
state_domains.migration: preserve normalized units, provider/tool source, estimate-versus-actual distinction and monotonic cumulative totals

state_domains.transaction_scope: terminal result + verification/receipt references committed with execution terminal fence
state_domains.consistency: at most one canonical final result per execution; OperationState may not become completed before the final result exists
state_domains.retention: operation/governance lifecycle controlled; artifacts/memory have their own referenced retention policies
state_domains.migration: preserve final status/output reference, verification, route/provider/tool receipts, usage, memory/artifact refs and terminal event identity

state_domains.consistency: thread owner/tenant binding and version are authoritative; client caches cannot advance thread state
state_domains.retention: governance controlled by thread retention class
state_domains.backup_restore: required with backend core application state
state_domains.migration: preserve thread_id, tenant/owner identity, status, active branch, version and retention metadata

state_domains.transaction_scope: idempotent exact message append and immutable lineage update
state_domains.consistency: message identity is immutable; branch sequence is monotonic; edit/regenerate creates lineage rather than overwriting canonical history
state_domains.retention: inherits/strengthens thread governance policy; referenced artifacts/memory have independent retention
state_domains.backup_restore: required with backend core application state
state_domains.migration: preserve message_id, thread/tenant/author identity, sequence, branch/supersedes lineage, operation/result refs and content/provenance refs

state_flows.rule: after convergence, Chroma receives indexable/minimized projection only; canonical writes commit to Mongo first
state_flows.failure: projection failure degrades retrieval but does not roll back already-committed canonical state

state_flows.rule: seed/content data may be re-indexed at any time
vector service stores retrievable projection with provenance/ACL metadata
state_flows.failure: degrade retrieval; never mutate canonical source to match index

state_flows.rule: engine vector index is derived from governed engine memory/content

operation state commits with a deterministic transactional outbox intent; a dispatcher appends the retry-stable outbox event to the canonical stream and acknowledges it only after durable stream acceptance
state_flows.failure: unpublished outbox rows remain recoverable work; transport events may not invent or advance operation state independently

state_flows.rule: snapshot is an explicit operator aid and never silently promoted to production authority
state_flows.failure: ignore/repair snapshot; authoritative state remains elsewhere

state_flows.rule: swarm scratch is materialized from admitted/running operation inputs and worker decomposition; it never becomes canonical operation or product state
state_flows.failure: discard or recompute scratch from the canonical operation/work request; never promote scratch after an ambiguous worker failure

state_flows.rule: one admitted OperationEnvelope binds to the canonical execution identity and checkpoint lineage; execution substate may refine but never contradict operation lifecycle state
state_flows.failure: checkpoint conflict or missing binding fails closed and the operation cannot advance to provider/tool execution

state_flows.rule: every side-effecting tool proposal obtains a durable call_id reservation before execution and commits a terminal receipt before the cognitive loop can reuse the result
state_flows.failure: ambiguous side effect enters reconciliation; blind replay is forbidden

state_flows.rule: approval-required actions persist an exact arguments digest and move the operation to waiting_for_user until a valid decision is committed
state_flows.failure: expired, mismatched or unauthorized approval leaves the action denied and resumable checkpoint intact

state_flows.rule: provider/tool/artifact boundaries append normalized actual usage deltas against the original execution budget without resetting consumed resources
state_flows.failure: unknown usage is recorded explicitly; policy may degrade or block further expensive work

state_flows.rule: verified final output and evidence references are committed before the enclosing operation transitions to completed
state_flows.failure: incomplete finalization remains recoverable and cannot emit a completed terminal event

state_flows.rule: message append authorizes against thread tenant/owner/status and uses thread version or exact-next sequence fencing
state_flows.failure: unauthorized, archived/deleting, stale-version or duplicate-conflict appends fail without mutating canonical history

state_flows.rule: a committed user message may create one or more explicitly identified execution branches; every assistant result binds back to the causal user message and thread
state_flows.failure: execution without a valid authorized causal message cannot be committed as a canonical conversation assistant response

state_flows.rule: a verified/qualified AIExecutionResult becomes an assistant message by immutable result reference plus allowed rendered content; message commit never fabricates a result identity
state_flows.failure: if assistant-message projection fails, the execution result remains authoritative and projection is retried idempotently

recovery_order: restore backend-core-app-state and any materialized engine authoritative state
restore conversation thread/message authority and verify branch/message ordering before accepting AI chat traffic
restore or reconstruct canonical operation state
restore cognitive execution, turn and checkpoint authority before resuming AI work
restore tool idempotency and human approval ledgers before allowing side-effect replay
restore execution usage and final AI result ledgers before terminal reconciliation
restore operation-event-stream only when it is configured as production authority
regenerate backend-seeded-content and swarm scratch as needed
rebuild Chroma/vector and process-memory projections from authoritative sources
treat snapshot files as optional recovery aids only
enable traffic only after authoritative stores are healthy and derived-store lag is within declared tolerance
invariants: authoritative and conditional-authoritative domains never use process-memory as their physical store
derived domains declare at least one upstream source and are rebuildable
mixed-transitional domains reference an open construction gap
authoritative durable domains require backup_restore and migration semantics
Chroma and in-process indexes are not the sole authority for canonical user, tenant, operation, or governance state
content and swarm logical databases are not included in canonical user-state migration merely because they share Mongo
operation-stream storage cannot claim production durability when running in-memory
authoritative-unbound domains are transitional only, production-ineligible, and must reference an open P0 gap
cognitive execution checkpoints, tool idempotency reservations, approvals, usage and final AI results cannot rely on process memory or client stream state
a completed operation requires an authoritative final AI result record when the operation used the cognitive runtime
approval decisions are bound to exact tool argument digests and cannot be replayed across edited calls
tool side-effect recovery consults the idempotency ledger before any retry
usage consumption is monotonic across retries, repairs and resumed turns
conversation thread/message authority is server-side durable state; client-submitted history never becomes authoritative by being sent to a model
assistant conversation messages reference canonical operation/execution results rather than treating provider text as standalone durable truth
conversation edit/regenerate preserves immutable branch lineage and never silently rewrites historical tool/action receipts
